lessons.title: Waqf signs in the mushaf
lessons.bigQuestion: 'Let's eat, Grandma' and 'Let's eat Grandma': one comma changes everything. How could a stop change the meaning of an ayah?
objectives: To understand the six main stopping signs of the Madinah mushaf and stop and restart correctly when reciting
successCriteria: All: name the six waqf signs and what they mean
Most: stop and restart (ibtida') correctly at ۖ and ۚ
Some: explain why the sign at 36:76 is lazim
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: protecting the meaning of Allah's words

keywords.def: reciting each letter with its right and its rules

hook.text: 'Let's eat, Grandma' and 'Let's eat Grandma': one comma changes everything. How could a stop change the meaning of an ayah?
hook.a: Stopping in the wrong place can join or split meanings wrongly; the waqf signs protect the meaning.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Knowing where to stop is part of tartil; the scholars of recitation placed small signs in the mushaf so readers stop where the meaning is complete.

starter.q: Recite Al-Mulk 67:2 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: The six signs
teach.note: Bismillah. These are the signs of the Madinah mushaf, written small above the line.

head: Sign
Name
Meaning
Example
rows: Must stop: joining would change the meaning
Stop at one of the two, not both

teach.heading: Why 36:76 is lazim
bullets: فَلَا يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ ۘ
Then: إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ ...
Joining would make 'We know ...' sound like their words
teach.note: The stop separates their speech from Allah's statement.

teach.heading: Stopping and restarting
bullets: Stop on a sukoon (tanween fathah becomes aa)
Restart from a sensible place
Never restart in the middle of a phrase
teach.note: Ibtida' (ابتداء): starting again. Model 67:3 stopping at ۖ, then starting at مَّا تَرَىٰ.

misconception.wrong: Stopping at ۙ (la) because you ran out of breath
misconception.right: Breathe earlier; at ۙ continue, or go back and restart

check.q: The sign ۘ (م) means ...
check.why: ۘ is waqf lazim: joining would give a wrong meaning.

practice.q: Read 2:2 «ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ ۛ فِيهِ ۛ هُدًۭى» and show the two allowed stops.
practice.a: Stop after رَيْبَ (then فِيهِ هُدًى joins), or after فِيهِ; never at both (mu'anaqah).
practice.model: I do: way 1: ... لَا رَيْبَ (stop), فِيهِ هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ. Way 2: ... لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ (stop), هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ. Not both.

practice.q: The stop sign صلى means ...

independent.q: Stretch: explain how a wrong stop could change a meaning, using 36:76.
independent.a: Joining قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ could suggest 'We know' is the disbelievers' saying.

lessons.title: Ayat al-Kursi: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Ayat al-Kursi (2:255) accurately
Identify rules in each phrase
Stop and start in sensible places

keywords.def: the Self-Sustaining, who sustains all things

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
What is the rule for noon before dhal?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
bullets: Allahu la ilaha illa huwa
Al-Hayyul-Qayyum
Teacher models; pupils echo
teach.note: Recite the opening: ٱللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ. Pupils echo phrase by phrase. This is a single long ayah in Surat Al-Baqarah, number 255. Many pupils know it already; focus on precision.

teach.heading: Phrase 1: rules
bullets: La ta'khudhuhu sinatun: silah sughra on hu
Sinatun wa la nawm: idghaam with ghunnah
Nawmun lahu: idghaam without ghunnah
teach.note: لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ: the haa between damma and sin gets silah sughra. سِنَةٌ وَلَا: tanween then waw, merge with ghunnah. نَوْمٌ لَّهُ: tanween then lam, merge without ghunnah. Ask pupils to say why each is different.

teach.heading: Phrase 2: rules
bullets: man dha: noon before dhal, ikhfa
'indahu illa: silah kubra, 4-5 counts
bi-idhnihi ya'lamu: silah sughra
teach.note: مَن ذَا: dhal is an ikhfa letter, so ikhfa. عِندَهُ إِلَّا: haa followed by hamzat qat', so silah kubra. بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ: haa after kasra then yaa voweled, silah sughra. Misconception: pupils think dhal is an idghaam letter.

teach.heading: Phrase 3: rules
bullets: shay'in min: idghaam with ghunnah
min 'ilmihi: izhar halqi
'ilmihi illa: silah kubra
teach.note: بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ: tanween then meem, idghaam bi-ghunnah. مِنْ عِلْمِهِ: noon sakinah before 'ayn, izhar. عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا: haa after kasra then hamzat qat', silah kubra. بِمَا شَاءَ: madd muttasil, 4-5 counts.

teach.heading: Last phrases
bullets: wasi'a kursiyyuhu as-samawat: no silah
wa la ya'uduhu hifzuhuma: silah sughra
al-'Aliyyul-'Azim: stop with madd 'arid
teach.note: كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ: the haa is followed by hamzat wasl, so no silah. This is a common error to correct. يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا: haa between two vowels, silah sughra. On stopping at الْعَظِيمُ, madd 'arid 2, 4 or 6, keep consistent.

practice: What rule applies to مَن ذَا?
Is there silah in كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ? Explain.
Which madd is in شَاءَ and how many counts?
independent: Recite the ayah in chunks, marking each rule
Record yourself and check against a model
Write the rule behind five words from the ayah
exit: Name one rule that gives silah kubra.
Why is there no silah in كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ?
lessons.homework: Learn Ayat al-Kursi securely and recite it to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and colour key for silah. Stretch: teach the silah rules to a partner with examples from the ayah.

lessons.title: Ayat al-Kursi: meaning and how tafsir works
objectives: Explain the main messages of Ayat al-Kursi
Describe the sources used in tafsir
Distinguish tafsir from personal reflection (tadabbur)

keywords.def: explanation of the meaning of the Qur'an by qualified scholars
reflecting on the Qur'an to apply its message

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.

teach.heading: The greatest ayah
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b
Which ayah is the greatest in the Book?
He answered: Ayat al-Kursi
teach.note: This is reported in Sahih Muslim: the Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b which ayah in the Book of Allah is the greatest, and Ubayy answered with Ayat al-Kursi. The Prophet ﷺ then struck his chest and prayed that knowledge would be easy for him. Keep the telling accurate and simple. Ask: why might this ayah be so central?

teach.heading: Phrase meanings (1)
bullets: No god but Allah, the Ever-Living, Self-Sustaining
Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him
To Him belongs all in the heavens and the earth
teach.note: Say each phrase slowly in English. Link al-Hayy to a life that never ends and al-Qayyum to the One who sustains everything. Ask: how is Allah's life different from ours? Reflect on dependence: we need rest; He does not.

teach.heading: Phrase meanings (2)
bullets: None can intercede except by His permission
He knows what is before and behind them
His knowledge is not encompassed except as He wills
teach.note: Intercession (shafa'ah) exists only by Allah's permission. Allah's knowledge covers everything; we know only what He lets us know. Misconception: shafa'ah does not belong to anyone independently. Ask: what does this teach us about humility?

teach.heading: Phrase meanings (3)
bullets: His Kursi extends over heavens and earth
Guarding them does not burden Him
He is the Most High, the Most Great
teach.note: Say that scholars have discussed what al-Kursi is; we accept what Allah has told us without trying to picture it. Ask: why does the ayah end with al-'Aliyy and al-'Azim? To remind us of Allah's greatness.

teach.heading: Tafsir and tadabbur
bullets: Tafsir uses the Qur'an and Sunnah
It also uses Companions' sayings and Arabic
Tadabbur is personal reflection after learning
See 38:29 on reflecting
teach.note: Teach the classical sources briefly: the Qur'an explains itself, the Sunnah, the understanding of the Companions, and Arabic language. Examples of well-known tafsir books: Tafsir al-Tabari, Tafsir Ibn Kathir. Quote 38:29: a blessed Book We have sent down so they may reflect on its ayat. Stress that tadabbur does not replace tafsir.

practice: Who may intercede, and on what condition?
independent: Write a one-line meaning for each phrase of Ayat al-Kursi
Draw a mind map of what the ayah teaches about Allah
Write a short tadabbur paragraph: how this ayah affects my day
exit: What is the difference between tafsir and tadabbur?
Which phrase of Ayat al-Kursi do you find most powerful?
lessons.homework: Write 120 words: what Ayat al-Kursi teaches about Allah and how it should shape my behaviour.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: phrase-by-phrase translation chart. Stretch: look up Ayat al-Kursi in a recognised tafsir and summarise one point.

lessons.title: Adab with the Qur'an
objectives: Describe the etiquette of reciting, listening and handling the Qur'an
Explain the reasons from the Qur'an
Make a personal adab plan

keywords.def: reciting slowly, clearly and with reflection
sincerity, doing something for Allah alone

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.

teach.heading: Before we recite
bullets: Make a sincere intention for Allah
Be in a clean, calm place
Seek refuge from Shaytan before reciting
teach.note: Cite 16:98: when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Discuss ikhlas: recite to please Allah, not to impress people. Ask: what can distract us when we recite?

teach.heading: Handling the mushaf
bullets: Hold it with respect
Keep it high and clean
The majority of scholars say wudu to touch it
teach.note: Pupils should not place the mushaf on the floor or under other items. Many scholars rely on 56:78-79 for the view that wudu is needed to touch the mushaf; practice varies between madhhabs, so ask your teacher or imam for the position you follow. Reading from a phone or tablet is a question for scholars, do not give a ruling.

teach.heading: Reciting well
bullets: Recite with tarteel: 73:4
Take care with tajweed
Do not rush; understand what you read
teach.note: Quote 73:4: and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation. Link this to Year 6 tarteel work. The Prophet ﷺ taught that the one who recites with difficulty has double reward (Bukhari and Muslim). Ask: how does this encourage those who find tajweed hard?

teach.heading: Listening
bullets: Listen in silence: 7:204
Give your full attention
Listening is also worship
teach.note: Read 7:204: when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy. Discuss real situations: a recitation on the speaker, a recital in class, a prayer. Ask: how do we show adab when we are listening?

teach.heading: Living by it
bullets: Reflect on it: 47:24
Practise what we learn
Each letter earns reward (Tirmidhi)
teach.note: 47:24: do they not reflect on the Qur'an, or are there locks on their hearts? A hadith in Tirmidhi says that whoever recites a letter of the Book of Allah receives a good deed, and each good deed is multiplied by ten. Link adab to action: reciting is not the end, acting is.

practice: Which ayah tells us to listen in silence?
Name two ways to respect the mushaf.
independent: Make a two-column list: adab before, during and after recitation
Write a personal plan for five daily minutes with the Qur'an
Role-play listening to a recitation with proper adab
exit: Write one adab you will start this week.
Which ayah supports reflecting on the Qur'an?
lessons.homework: Follow your personal adab plan for five days and note how it feels.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: illustrated adab checklist. Stretch: research how one of the four madhhabs views handling the mushaf.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Mulk 67:1-4: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Al-Mulk ayat 1-4 accurately
Identify rules in each ayah
Use consistent stops and madd lengths
starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Which rule applies when noon sakinah meets qaf?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
bullets: Surat Al-Mulk is Surah 67
We study the first four ayat
Echo the teacher in short phrases
teach.note: Recite ayah 1: تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ. Pupils echo. Explain that Al-Mulk has 30 ayat and we begin with the first four.

teach.heading: Ayah 1 rules
bullets: bi-yadihil-mulk: no silah, hamzat wasl follows
shay'in qadir: tanween before qaf, ikhfa
Stop on qadir: madd 'arid
teach.note: بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ: the haa is followed by the alif of al-, a hamzat wasl, so no silah. شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: tanween before qaf is ikhfa. At the stop, the yaa is followed by a stop-sakin raa: madd 'arid. Ask pupils to say why the first haa is short.

teach.heading: Ayah 2 rules
bullets: al-mawta wal-hayata: lam qamariyyah
'amalan: madd 'iwad at a stop
al-'Azizul-Ghafur: stop with madd 'arid
teach.note: الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَيَاةَ: both lams are qamariyyah, since meem and haa are moon letters. Practise stopping on عَمَلًا: the tanween becomes an alif, 2 counts. Common error: pupils stop with tanween sound.

teach.heading: Ayah 3 rules
bullets: tibaqan: stop with madd 'iwad
min tafawut: noon before taa, ikhfa
min futur: noon before faa, ikhfa
teach.note: مِن تَفَاوُتٍ: ta is an ikhfa letter. مِن فُطُورٍ: faa is an ikhfa letter. Ask pupils to list all ikhfa letters (15) and check both appear. تَرَىٰ: the alif maqsurah is madd tabi'i, 2 counts.

teach.heading: Ayah 4 rules
bullets: thumma irji'il-basar: join the hamzat wasl
yanqalib: noon before qaf, ikhfa
khasi'an wa huwa: idghaam with ghunnah
teach.note: ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ: when joining, we drop the hamzat wasl: thummarji'. يَنقَلِبْ: ikhfa before qaf. خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ: tanween then waw, idghaam bi-ghunnah. On stopping at حَسِيرٌ, madd 'arid. Peer-check each rule.

practice: Why is there no silah in بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ?
Which rule applies to مِن تَفَاوُتٍ?
How do you read طِبَاقًا when stopping?
independent: Recite ayat 1-4 three times, marking each rule
Record and compare with a model recitation
Write the rule behind six words
exit: Name one ikhfa example in the passage.
Explain madd 'iwad with an example from the passage.
lessons.homework: Memorise ayat 1-4 of Surat Al-Mulk.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio, colour-coded rule key. Stretch: explain the stop rules to a partner without notes.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Mulk 67:1-4: meaning and memory plan
objectives: Explain the meaning of ayat 1-4
Reflect on purpose in life and death
Plan revision using a new-recent-old cycle

keywords.def: new lesson, recent revision, older revision

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.

teach.heading: Ayat 1-2: Sovereignty and purpose
bullets: Blessed is He in whose hand is all dominion
He created death and life
To test which of you is best in deeds
teach.note: Read 67:2 slowly. The word is ahsanu 'amalan, best in deeds, not most deeds. Ask: what makes a deed best? Sincerity and being correct are the usual answers given by scholars. Link to ikhlas from last lesson.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-4: Look again
bullets: Seven heavens, one above another
You will not see any flaw in the Merciful's creation
Look again: your sight returns dazzled and weary
teach.note: Read 67:3-4. The surah invites us to observe: look again, and again, you will find no flaw. Ask: what in nature gives you awe? Bring in tafsir carefully: scholars explain 'khasi'an' as sight returning humbled and 'hasir' as exhausted.

teach.heading: Tadabbur questions
bullets: What is my test in life?
How do I respond to the beauty of creation?
What action follows?
teach.note: Pupils answer in pairs. Possible responses: study well, treat people kindly, thank Allah for creation. Remind them that the aim is to link meaning to action. Do not push controversial interpretations; rely on tafsir.

teach.heading: A revision system
bullets: Sabaq: today's new lines
Sabqi: the last few days' lines
Manzil: older surahs, cycled weekly
teach.note: Introduce the three-part system used by many memorisers: sabaq (new), sabqi (recent), manzil (older). Pupils map their own surahs onto it: Al-Ma'un, At-Takathur, Al-'Asr, Al-Humazah, Al-Fil, Al-Mulk. Ask: how often should each be revised?

teach.heading: My plan
bullets: Write a two-week schedule
Include five minutes per day
Revise with a partner weekly
teach.note: Pupils write a two-week revision plan. Remind them that consistency beats long sessions. Share a few examples. Close with a dua to keep what we have learned.

practice: What is the meaning of ahsanu 'amalan?
Why does the surah tell us to look again?
What do sabaq, sabqi and manzil mean?
independent: Write the meaning of each ayah in your own words
exit: Which of your surahs is in sabqi this week?
lessons.homework: Follow your revision plan and tick off each day.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: translation chart with key words and a visual plan template. Stretch: compare 67:2 with another ayah on trials.

lessons.title: Recital assessment 1: Ya-Sin against the rubric

independent.q: Stretch: why is the alif in «ٱلْقُرْءَانِ» only 2 counts though a hamza is near?
independent.a: The hamza comes before the madd letter (madd badal), not after it, so it stays 2.

objectives: To understand the feedback from my recital and plan how to act on it
successCriteria: All: read my rubric feedback and name one strength
Most: turn each weak row into an action
Some: link my actions to a weekly routine
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: humility in accepting correction

keywords.def: information about how well I did and what to improve
revising memorised Qur'an so it stays firm

hook.text: Feedback can feel uncomfortable. Why is it a gift?
hook.a: It shows exactly what to fix; the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions corrected one another's recitation with care.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?' (Al-Qamar 54:17).

starter.q: A rubric row 'Fluency and waqf' covers ...
Recite Ya-Sin 36:80 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Reading your rubric
teach.note: Bismillah. Each pupil opens their own feedback in the portal; no sharing of marks.

head: Feedback
Action
rows: 3-3-link those ayat daily for a week
Tahqiq drill on one page a day
Add 3 surahs to the manzil each day

teach.heading: Reflection
bullets: What went well?
What surprised me?
What will I change?

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: The best response to 'ghunnah uneven' is ...
options: a daily slow drill on a page
check.why: A specific action.

practice.q: Turn this feedback into an action: 'Hesitates at section joins in Ya-Sin'.
practice.a: Learn the first words of each section as a chain and recite the joins daily.
practice.model: I do: 'Madd munfasil inconsistent' becomes 'tap 4 counts on every munfasil in Ya-Sin 1 to 12 this week'.

independent.q: In the portal response box: write a reflection on your recital and three actions linked to your rubric rows. Today's group re-recites the passage they found hardest.
independent.a: Three specific actions linked to feedback.
independent.model: The teacher shows a model reflection (no real pupil data).

independent.q: Extend: listen to the teacher recite 36:79 to 83 and check your home hifdh.
independent.a: Home hifdh checked.

independent.q: Stretch: mark the waqf signs in 36:68 to 83.

exit.q: My actions are saved ...
exit.a: in the portal

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Feedback can feel uncomfortable. Why is it a gift?
exit.a: It shows exactly what to fix; the Prophet ﷺ and the Companions corrected one another's recitation with care.

lessons.homework: Start your three actions this week; tick the revision log.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.

lessons.title: Targets for Year 11 and the summer revision plan
lessons.bigQuestion: Year 11 brings exams. How will you make sure the Qur'an stays first, not last?
objectives: To understand how to set Qur'an targets for Year 11 and plan revision so Ya-Sin, Juz' 29 and 30 stay firm
successCriteria: All: write two Year 11 targets
Most: build a summer manzil covering Ya-Sin and Juz' 29 and 30
Some: plan how Qur'an fits alongside GCSE revision next year
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: putting Allah's Book first

keywords.def: a fixed daily portion of revision
revising memorised Qur'an so it stays firm
a specific next step with a way to check it

hook.text: Year 11 brings exams. How will you make sure the Qur'an stays first, not last?
hook.a: A fixed daily time (for example after Fajr), short and consistent, and reciting in salah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things, and to Him you will be returned.' (Ya-Sin 36:83).

starter.q: Recite Ya-Sin 36:81 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Summer manzil
teach.note: Bismillah.

teach.heading: Year 11 preview
bullets: Tajweed mastery
Al-Kahf consolidation
Understanding and teaching others

teach.heading: Qur'an and exams
bullets: Qur'an first, short and daily
Recite in salah
Du'a before study
teach.note: The teacher closes with du'a for the class.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: The best way to protect Qur'an time in Year 11 is ...
check.why: Consistency over intensity.

practice.q: Write one Year 11 Qur'an target that is specific and checkable.
practice.a: For example: 'Recite Ya-Sin in full each Friday with no prompts by December.'
practice.model: I do: 'Revise Juz' 29 every fortnight with a listener.'

independent.q: Complete the summer manzil and Year 11 targets in the portal; share one strategy (not marks) in the chat.
independent.a: A complete plan and two targets.
independent.model: The teacher shows a completed plan.

independent.q: Extend: plan to read the tafsir of Ya-Sin 77 to 83 from a trusted source.
independent.a: A plan.

independent.q: Stretch: plan a weekly full recital of Ya-Sin.
independent.a: A day chosen.

exit.q: Ya-Sin ends with: 'to Him you will be ...'
exit.a: returned

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Year 11 brings exams. How will you make sure the Qur'an stays first, not last?
exit.a: A fixed daily time (for example after Fajr), short and consistent, and reciting in salah.

lessons.homework: Share the plan with your parents and begin the summer manzil.
